summary: A 1954 L-4 cab on a concrete block tower that replaced earlier lookouts on St. Joe Baldy, now stripped of its catwalk and used as a communications vault.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 10-foot concrete block tower
facts.status_note: Catwalk, shutters, and stairs removed; the cab is now used as a communications vault rather than a staffed lookout.

access.note: Now active communications infrastructure with its exterior access features removed; not set up for public climbing.

facts.agency: US Forest Service / Idaho Department of Lands

events.note: A Forest Service camp was established on the summit in the 1920s.
A wooden L-4 cab was built on the summit.
The current L-4 cab on a 10-foot concrete block tower was built on a nearby summit about a mile southwest, replacing the earlier lookout.
The lookout has not been staffed since the 1980s.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on December 5, 2020.
Mr. and Mrs. Warren Hollenbeck listed as lookout personnel.

evidence.quote: St Joe Baldy was first a forest service camp in the 1920.

evidence.supports: 1954 replacement structure built a mile southwest
evidence.quote:
St. Joe Baldy was constructed in 1954 replacing an earlier lookout site about a mile away.
A Region 1/L-4 cabin was placed atop a 10 foot block tower.
On Sunday, Mrs. Molly Frenger accompanied Mr. and Mrs Bob Larson on a trip to St Maries, where Mr. Larson is building a Lookout station for the forestry department.

1960
Mr. & Mrs. Warren Hollenbeck (Kellogg Evening News)
Known lookout personnel: 1960: Mr. and Mrs. Warren Hollenbeck.

evidence.supports: 1960 newspaper mention of continued lookout value
evidence.quote: It will include a high lookout atop St. Joe Baldy and will mean $2,000 extra revenue yearly.

evidence.supports: unstaffed since 1980s, now a comms vault
evidence.quote: The lookout has not been staffed since the 1980's. The catwalk, shutters and stairs have been removed. The structure is now used as a communications vault.

sources.title: St. Joe Baldy Fire Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: Build-year chronology (1920s camp -> 1935 L-4 -> 1954 current cab) is consistent across sources. Fact-check (2026-10-04) found the original 'Hollenbeck in 1932 vs 1960' conflict was an error: the 1932 entry on idahofirelookouts.com belongs to a different person (Herb Uttley), and both Idaho Fire Lookouts and Firelookout.com actually date the Hollenbecks to 1960. The story and this file were corrected to drop the false conflict. No source gives current public-access status beyond 'used as a communications vault', so access is inferred as restricted rather than confirmed closed/open.
